notes: Read SKILL.md (397 lines) in full. Explains and configures browser security headers (CSP, X-Frame-Options DENY, nosniff, production-only HSTS, X-Robots-Tag on /dashboard) in a Next.js clerkMiddleware, with the complete middleware.ts code included (SKILL.md:195-250), so it is self-contained apart from the Clerk/Convex/Stripe stack it assumes.

Following it, the agent edits middleware.ts and may run 'curl -I' against localhost or the user's own deployed site and suggest online header checkers; no installs, secrets or remote scripts. CSP origins are built from public NEXT_PUBLIC_* environment variables, not secrets.

Security caveats a user should know: the default script-src includes 'unsafe-inline' and 'unsafe-eval' (SKILL.md:60, 214); the trade-off is disclosed (94) and a nonce-based alternative is offered (334-338), but with these directives CSP gives little XSS protection, so the claims that CSP would have stopped Magecart (27) and that connect-src prevents data exfiltration 'even if XSS bypasses sanitization' (97, 367) are overstated (img-src allows any https: origin). Prefer the nonce approach where possible.

Minor inaccuracies: the nosniff example (133-139) implies an tag could execute script; the Scott Helme statistic (24) is unverified; includeSubDomains HSTS should be enabled only once all subdomains serve HTTPS.
